checklist.detail: Stainless Steel (304/316): only 15% thermal margin (computed wall temp 959 K vs 1100 K max). Thin margin. Basis: coupled throat wall balance: gas h_g ~6.6 kW/m2K incl. carbon-deposit credit, T_aw ~3588 K, coolant ~36 m/s (coolant-side wall ~741 K), 0.20 mm wall. Levers that lower it: faster coolant (Coolant velocity; SP-8087 caps liquids at ~61 m/s, at a jacket-dP cost), a thinner wall, a liner rated hotter or more conductive (e.g. GRCop-84), or more film cooling.

checklist.detail: Hottest wall station is in the convergent section (area ratio ~1.2, regen): wall ~978 K, 1.12x that section's material limit (warns below 1.15x, like the throat row). Levers: more chamber film (or a convergent film ring for the throat region), faster coolant, a thinner or more conductive liner, or extend active cooling.

checklist.detail: OK - primary hoop stress ~64 MPa (~8.3 MPa net jacket-vs-gas differential, Huzel eq 4-27/4-28, tube_wall) vs a ~67 MPa allowable at the end of active cooling (area ratio ~14.0) (Stainless Steel (304/316), SF 1.5, wall ~0.32 mm). The thermal-restraint stress (~511 MPa at the throat, dT = q*t/k across the wall) is a self-limiting secondary stress, not a burst load: with the hoop load it exceeds Stainless Steel (304/316)'s ~100 MPa hot yield, so the hot face yields a little each firing - expected for a regen tube wall (the real F-1/J-2/RL10 do the same in this model). Its life limit is the 'Throat thermal-fatigue cycle life' row.
